name: manual_f445c8
claim: A cached path/config file (like .paths.ps1) written on a broken first run can permanently shadow a later fix unless the code explicitly re-validates the cached value against current reality and force-rewrites the cache when they diverge — just fixing the underlying bug isn't enough if something else still trusts the stale cache.

decisions.notes: After adding a bootstrap that creates a missing venv for Perpetua-Tools, start.ps1 still failed the same way on the next run because .paths.ps1 had cached the old dep-less system-Python path from before the venv existed, and the loader only skipped re-resolution when a cached value was already present. Fixed by always preferring the freshly-verified venv path over the cached one and forcing a cache rewrite when they differ.
